The story follows a group of rebels on a dangerous mission to steal the plans for the Death Star. Felicity Jones stars as a rebel soldier in this anthology film.

Tehran, Iran (CNN) -- A Persian proverb says a good year depends on its spring. For many Iranians, the historic decision by Tehran and six world powers -- the United States, Britain, France, Germany, Russia and China -- to continue nuclear negotiations under a "joint comprehensive plan of action" is an indication that this year's Norouz, the Persian New Year that started on March 21, will be a superb one indeed. Although some hardliners may complain the preliminary agreement is not what they hoped, for many people it shows excellent progress and that's what they want.

Ferguson, Missouri (CNN) Two African-American candidates, Ella Jones and Wesley Bell, won seats on the Ferguson City Council on Tuesday. This means three of the six council members are now black.

The election took place on Tuesday. It began at 6 a.m. despite rainy weather and flood warnings. This was the first city election since a white police officer shot and killed an unarmed black teenager named Michael Brown last August. Before this, very few people traditionally voted in these municipal elections.

An Israeli man was killed and a woman was hurt when a 37-year-old Arab driver from East Jerusalem hit them at a bus stop in the French Hill section of Jerusalem Wednesday night. Police say it was a suspected terror attack. The driver was arrested and is being investigated by the General Security Services. One of the victims, Shalom Yohai Cherki, 26, died at the hospital. The woman, 20, is still in serious condition.

A collection of art owned by the late actress Lauren Bacall was sold in New York on March 31. The collection includes works by famous 20th-century artists. It had been shown in Hong Kong, Paris, London, and Los Angeles before the sale. Bacall, who died in 2014 at age 89, became famous in 1944 with the film "To Have And Have Not." She also met her husband, Humphrey Bogart, that year. At the 2015 Golden Globes, George Clooney honored her in his speech.

Kiev, Ukraine (CNN)
The question on people's minds in Kiev right now is: Who might be killing allies of Ukraine's ousted President Viktor Yanukovych?

This idea is not brand new. But it came to the front again this week with two high-profile shooting deaths in the Ukrainian capital. One was a former member of parliament with ties to Yanukovych. The other was a Ukrainian journalist known for his pro-Russian views.

Oleg Kalashnikov, the former member of parliament, was shot and killed shortly after 7 p.m. Wednesday at the entrance to his apartment block.

CNN) Chile will soon recognize civil unions for same-sex couples. President Michelle Bachelet signed a new law on Monday that allows same-sex and opposite-sex couples to register their relationships. "This is a concrete step in the drive to end the difference between homosexual and heterosexual couples," Bachelet said. The law will officially start in six months. The government estimates about 2 million people will benefit from this change.

The next time you fly to Florida to visit Grandma, or take the kids to see the "talking mouse" or go to South Beach for sun and fun, look out your window before landing. The Everglades swamp below looks like a dangerous, useless wasteland full of things that can hurt you: snakes, scorpions, rats, roaches, gators, and mosquitoes. A researcher once caught 365,000 bloodthirsty bugs in one trap in one night. While it may look like a waste of man's efforts, the Everglades represents both man's folly and the cost of redemption.

CNN reports that ISIS militants took control of Yarmouk, a Palestinian refugee camp near Damascus, after defeating other militia groups there. The camp had been under siege and bombardment by Syrian forces for over two years. A resident told CNN that the militants "slaughtered" people in the streets, including three men who were caught and killed in front of others. The Islamic State now controls almost all of the camp.

China's government has long blocked its citizens from reading Western news websites using a "Great Firewall." But a new study says this is no longer enough. China has now attacked servers outside its borders, including in the United States. The study's authors have named this new weapon the "Great Cannon." It operates openly. The authors warn that attacking another country so visibly will likely cause international anger, but China may have counted on that.

A German official said investigators still do not know why co-pilot Andreas Lubitz crashed Germanwings Flight 9525. However, the official said Lubitz had suicidal thoughts at some point before he became a pilot. Investigators have not found any notes or conversations explaining his motives. Medical records also show that Lubitz was suicidal and received therapy before he ever got his pilot's license.

The leader of Yemen's Houthi rebels said on Sunday that his group will not give up. This came after a top Saudi military official said that weeks of airstrikes had hurt the Shiite group.

In a televised address, rebel leader Abdul-Malik al-Houthi stated that his fighters would not leave the main cities or government institutions. "Anyone who thinks we will surrender is dreaming," he said.

His comments came after more than three weeks of Saudi-led coalition bombings. The bombings began after the Houthis surged into the capital of Sanaa in January and ousted President Abdu Rabu Mansour Hadi from power.

On April 19, 1995, Timothy McVeigh exploded a truck bomb in front of the Murrah Federal Building in Oklahoma City. The attack killed 168 people and injured hundreds more. It remains the deadliest act of domestic terrorism in U.S. history.

The attack shocked the country. It was not just the scale of the tragedy that drew attention, but the fact that American citizens were targeting their own government with a deadliness hitherto unseen.

If you care deeply about something, you might protest, make a sign, or join a demonstration. How long can you keep going for, in the face of indifference and inaction?

More than 200 Nigerian girls were kidnapped from their school a year ago by Boko Haram militants. Millions of people around the world joined a social media campaign to plead for their safe return. Charles Alasholuyi was one of those people -- from celebrities to world leaders -- voicing their anger via #BringBackOurGirls, one of the top Twitter hashtags of 2014, used in more than four million tweets.

But as weeks turned into months, there was still no sign of the missing girls. The spotlight on the campaign faded.

Barney Frank, a retired congressman, recently spoke in Chicago. He entertained a sold-out crowd at the Center on Halsted while discussing his 45 years in public service. Frank made history as the first member of Congress to marry someone of the same-sex while in office. He also had strong opinions about closeted politicians who vote against LGBT rights. When asked about a California ballot proposal that would legalize killing gay people, Frank said he was not aware of the measure but told the young man not to worry about "c crazy people."

CNN reports that a brutal attack on Garissa University College in Kenya left about 150 people dead, including students, and dozens more wounded. Gunmen attacked the campus early Thursday during morning prayers, shooting randomly and taking hostages before being killed by security forces. The U.S. Embassy in Nairobi said Al-Shabaab militants claimed responsibility. The attack comes just months after Al-Shabaab militants murdered non-Muslim workers in a Kenyan quarry. The terrorist group has been behind numerous attacks in the region and has also recruited some Americans, particularly from the Somali-American community in Minnesota.

Students at the University of Cape Town in South Africa have successfully removed a statue of Cecil Rhodes. The students had protested for weeks, saying the British colonialist's legacy was racist. The university said the heritage authority allowed them to take the statue down to keep it safe while they decide what to do with it next.

Syria is a very dangerous place. A group that opposes the government says many people have died there. Since the civil war started, 310,000 people have been killed. One year ago, 162,402 people had been killed. The United Nations says the number was 70,000 the year before that. Over half of all Syrians are very poor and need help to survive. The United Nations says food rations are being cut because people are not giving enough donations.

CNN reports that Ailina Tsarnaeva was not shy when threatening a woman she considered a rival. According to a criminal complaint, Tsarnaeva called the woman and said, "Leave my man alone" and warned, "Stop looking for him. ... I know people that can put a bomb where you live." Prosecutors did not view this as a joke and charged her with aggravated harassment, a charge she denies. Tsarnaeva is the sister of Dzhokhar and Tamerlan Tsarnaev.

A Gaza police official said on Thursday that police took a door with a drawing by the artist Banksy. The owner, Rabea Darduna, said he sold the door for $175 because he did not know how valuable it was. The door will stay with the police until a court hearing. Darduna said that when his home was destroyed last summer, he felt he had nothing left. He only had a doorway and a door.

A Saudi-led coalition is attacking Houthi rebels in Yemen. Five days after the first airstrikes, the coalition says it now has control of the area. Locals are fleeing the fighting, and many civilians have been killed. The coalition has destroyed most of the Houthi air defense systems and air bases. Saudi Arabia's navy is blocking Yemeni ports, only allowing closely watched medical goods to enter.

Holland manager Guus Hiddink was very angry at his own fans for booing Andres Iniesta during the 2-0 victory against Spain on Tuesday. Spain coach Vicente del Bosque had an experimental side, and Iniesta, who started on the bench, came into the game in the 76th minute. The home fans jeered and booed him. Centre back Stefan de Vrij and midfielder Davy Klaassen scored first-half goals in the victory, but Hiddink was unimpressed with the way Iniesta was treated. Spain midfielder Andres Iniesta controls the ball during his side's 2-0 defeat by Holland on Tuesday night.

Scotland will find out on May 21 if their game against Georgia in September will be played without fans in the stadium. UEFA, European football's governing body, has started disciplinary proceedings against the Georgian Football Federation. This happened after fans ran onto the field twice during Sunday's 2-0 game between Germany and Georgia in Tbilisi. UEFA is also going to look at other charges. These charges say home fans set off fireworks. They also say there were safety breaches, like blocked stairs, locked gates, and a lack of body searches by staff at the Boris Paichadze Stadium.

Football agents were unsure about their future on Wednesday while waiting for new rules to be announced. Starting April 1st, anyone will be able to become a football agent by paying £500 for a one-year registration. The FA will then charge £250 every year to renew the license. Agents who already have a license are exempt from these new rules. The FA was expected to put a link on their website for agents to sign up, but as of 1pm, that link had not appeared. Mel Stein believes the new rules will "create anarchy." These new guidelines started after FIFA decided they would no longer govern agents.

CSKA Sofia's Latvian goalkeeper Maksims Uvarenko has not been paid for three months. He has had to ask his parents to send him money to pay his rent. Despite these financial problems, Uvarenko, who joined the Bulgarian club in January, is impressed by the club's unique and passionate fans. He told local media that the lack of money is the biggest problem he has faced at CSKA, as he still hasn't received his salary.

David Moore, 25, got very angry on the road right after he left his house. He got stuck in heavy traffic right next to Rafal Cegielka, 45, who was picking up his child from school. Moore then punched the father and smashed his car with a hockey stick while children watched, because he was having a "bad day" and saw red.

Spain lost 2-0 to Holland on Tuesday. This defeat reminded coach Vicente del Bosque of their bad 2014 World Cup performance. Gerard Pique says the coach is not too worried about a third straight friendly loss. In the group stage last year at Brazil, Holland beat Spain 5-1, ending Spain's six-year domination. Holland scored two early goals at the Amsterdam Arena and held on despite strong pressure from Spain in the second half.

A New York City mother and her daughter have fled to Germany during a custody battle, police say. Ulrike Berger, 44, is not allowed to leave the country with her seven-year-old daughter, Kaia. However, on March 22, a day after the girl was dropped off for a weekend visit, they are believed to have boarded a plane to Europe.

Police are searching for Ulrike Berger, 44, and her seven-year-old daughter Kaia. It is believed the pair boarded a plane from New York to Germany on March 22, violating a custody court order. Police say the pair were last seen at Berger's home in Boerun Hill, Brooklyn, at 10am on March 21, when Kaia's father dropped

A huge fire ripped through dry heathland near the south coast. The fire looked like a disaster movie as it destroyed an area the size of 100 football pitches. It happened after days of storms hit Britain, which had felled trees and shut roads.

However, the 70-hectare area of Dorset was very dry because much of it is on a hillside, and water had run off down the slope. Fire investigators confirmed the fire was started deliberately. Three separate areas of heath—half a hectare, one hectare, and 70 hectares—were destroyed.

Last night, emergency services were very busy. They received about 600 calls every hour because people were drinking heavily to celebrate the New Year. Parmedics were extremely busy, and in Cambridge, a military hospital was set up to help people who were drunk.

In London, the ambulance service said at the busiest time they were getting over 600 calls an hour—more than three times the normal amount.

In Manchester, a man fell down on the pavement near an ambulance while people walked past eating food. In Manchester, another man was slumped over in a doorway while women celebrated the New Year.

Liverpool goalkeeper Simon Mignolet said his mental strength helped him recover after being dropped in December. The manager had dropped him indefinitely due to poor form, but he returned quickly when Brad Jones got hurt. Mignolet told a magazine that he stayed positive despite the disappointment.

Giant hailstones the size of plums fell over the South on Tuesday. Residents rushed outside to record the strange weather. A Twitter user named Arke USA from Bryant, Arkansas, filmed the ice balls hitting his backyard and making a loud "plop" sound as they landed in the swimming pool. The footage shows the hailstones falling quickly, with many cracking upon impact. Despite the temperature being around 80 degrees, the compacted lumps are resilient to the heat and take a while to melt. In seconds, the patio is completely covered in white pellets.

A replica pirate ship called the Liana's Ransom ran into trouble about 30 miles off the coast of Maine on Monday. The crew reported that their engine failed and the sails got tangled up on the mast. Because of the rough seas, nine people were lifted off the ship by Coast Guard boats and brought to safety. The ship was left drifting in the water.

Amazing pictures have emerged of blue fluorescent algae lighting up Australia's east coast. The images were taken in Jervis Bay, on the south coast of New South Wales, as the neon glow illuminated one of Australia's popular beaches. Photographer Andy Hutchinson described the sight as a 'be beautiful supernatural scene' caused by millions of plankton omitting light. A similar display was shown in Sydney's Manly Beach back in August 2014 where an oceanography expert told Daily Mail Australia there was no need to be concerned about the algae.

A 17-year-old boy named Rahul Kumar climbed over a fence into a lion enclosure at a zoo in Ahmedabad. He was drunk and shouting that he would kill the animals. Zoo security had to rescue him after he ran towards the lions.

A 12-year-old boy fell out of a five-story window and survived by landing on a car parked below. His father says he likely fell while sleepwalking. The accident happened last Saturday in Nanchang, China. A hotel worker across the road said she heard a loud noise around midnight and thought it was a car crash.

Red Wings player Drew Miller is happy to be back on the ice just one day after getting a deep cut on his face. He feels very lucky the skate did not hit his eye. He had a bad-looking scar across his eye, but the reports say he did not lose any eyesight. He needed 50 to 60 stitches to close the wound.

Filipe Luis says he wants to stay at Chelsea until his contract ends, even though Atletico Madrid wants to sign him back in the summer. He signed a three-year deal last July, but has had a hard time playing at the left back position at Stamford Bridge. Atletico hope this may give them leverage, but Luis said: ‘I’m happy at Chelsea. I want to stay at the club until the end of my contract.’
A 20-year-old fan ran onto the pitch during a soccer game and did flips. He was banned for three years for his actions.

A video shows a van carrying football fans swerving around a corner in Salé, Morocco. About half a dozen people were sitting on the roof of the vehicle. As the van moved at high speed, it tipped over to one side, sending the riders flying. The footage was taken from a car following the van.

England have been drawn in Group D with the Republic of Ireland, Holland, and Italy at the UEFA Under 17 European Championships in Bulgaria this May.

John Peacock's Young Lions are the defending champions after winning last year's final in Malta on penalties against Holland. To reach the quarter-finals, they must overcome the Dutch again.

This tournament is the first to expand from eight to 16 nations. Danny Collinge scored his first England goal in qualifying.

An angry elephant tried to spray a buffalo bull with water because the bull got too close. The elephant was relaxing in Kruger National Park in South Africa with its family by a small pool of water. In a video, the elephant squits water from its trunk at the bull, but misses. The frustrated elephant tries again to spray the bull, but its young calf comes close for safety as the bull drinks water.

Michael Thorpe, a former pub landlord, has had his conviction overturned after an eight-year legal fight. He was found guilty in 2006 for showing a Premier League match on foreign TV channels at his Plymouth pub. Mr. Thorpe, 55, says the legal battle cost him his business and his reputation.

The Irish Football Association is worried that damage at its Windsor Park home in Belfast might stop the team from playing a crucial Euro 2016 qualifier against Romania in June. Cracks appeared in the West Stand on Tuesday morning, and the area was closed off while engineers checked it. The Irish FA learned on Tuesday morning that overnight damage had happened to the West Stand of the National Football Stadium at Windsor Park. Northern Ireland's Windsor Park had overnight damage to its West Stand on Monday night.

A 20-year-old football fan has been banned for three years after running onto the pitch and doing somersaults during his first visit to the stadium. Charlie Sumner invaded the field at Reading's Madejski Stadium during an FA Cup replay with Bradford City. While his team was 3-0 up, Sumner did four front flips before being tackled by stewards.

A man driving a BMW car with five children inside was arrested today. He is suspected of knocking down and killing Hina Shamim, a 21-year-old student. Miss Shamim died near the University of Kingston in London last night. She was just weeks away from turning 22. Friends left flowers at the scene. They said Miss Shamim, who was from Peterborough, was "much-loved and the most charming lovely girl in the world." She was killed while walking a short distance from home to the library.

A mother and her teenage daughter were arrested after a video of them fighting with a student at a high school was posted online. The incident happened at Langham Creek High School in Houston on Tuesday. The mother was angry because she said the girl had been bullying her daughter. In the video, the mother is seen wearing a black top on the right side, and the student she is fighting with is in the center wearing white.

Stoke chief executive Tony Scholes wants to keep goalkeeper Asmir Begovic. Begovic has one year left on his contract and has been linked with other clubs. Scholes believes Stoke can meet Begovic's ambitions. He said Begovic is a terrific goalkeeper and they want to keep him.

A bus driver in Auckland, New Zealand was filmed reading a newspaper while driving. A passenger sent the video to the bus company, Ritchies Coachlines. In the video, the driver is seen flicking through the paper while the bus moves. When the bus slows down for traffic lights, he moves his head to read one of the pages. The bus company boss, Andrew Ritchie, called the driver a "complete idiot" and said he was embarrassed by the driver's actions.

West Ham manager Sam Allardyce says Winston Reid will play on Saturday against Leicester City. Reid injured his hamstring in a game against Chelsea on March 4, but he is fully fit now. However, Enner Valencia will not play. Valencia missed the last two games because of a toe injury he got at home in mid-March, but the manager says he is not match fit yet.

Five days before their wedding last May, a car crash killed Brittany Huber and left her fiancé, John Redman, fighting for his life. Redman survived the accident, but doctors told him he would likely spend the rest of his life in a nursing home, confined to a wheelchair. Despite these odds, Redman recovered. On March 24, the 25-year-old basketball coach at Dalton State College helped lead his team to a championship.

Lucas (left) and Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard before Sunday's All-Star charity game at Anfield.

Liverpool midfielder Lucas Leiva is trying to return to his best form after recovering from injury. The Brazil international started 16 games in 19 matches from late November. This run coincided with a marked improvement in the team's results, until a groin problem in February's Merseyside derby saw him miss 10 games.

He was an unused substitute in the defeat by Manchester United immediately before the international break, their first in the league since mid-December, but played 90 minutes in Sunday's All-Star Charity game at Anfield.
Japanese photographer Yûki Aoyama takes pictures of fathers jumping into the air while their daughters smile at the camera. He published these photos in a new book called "Daughter and Salary Man."

Police are looking for a man between 50 and 60 years old. He is suspected of robbing a bank in broad daylight and taking £3,000 in cash.

The robbery happened at 12:30pm at a Lloyds Bank branch in Fairwater, Cardiff. Officials have released CCTV images of the suspect. He is between 5ft 9in and 6ft tall and was wearing black clothing.

The white male suspect has greying black hair and wore glasses. He was captured on camera inside the bank. Officials said no one was injured during the robbery and they were confident the public would be able to identify him.

The Court of Arbitration for Sport has allowed Morocco to compete in the next two African Cup of Nations tournaments. Morocco was originally banned from the 2017 and 2019 tournaments and fined $1 million by the Confederation of African Football after they pulled out because of the Ebola epidemic. The CAF had also demanded $9 million in compensation. Morocco can now compete in the tournaments after the ban was lifted.

Tom Boyd thinks Jason Denayer has done such a good job on loan at Celtic that he is ready to fight for a spot at Manchester City next year. This would stop Celtic manager Ronny Deila from keeping the young Belgian for another year, but Boyd thinks this is still good news. He believes Denayer’s success can show other young players that moving to Celtic is a great next step in their career. Young defender Jason Denayer has impressed on loan at Celtic this season. The 19-year-old recently won his first international cap for Belgium in a Euro 2016 qualifier against Cyprus.

Andros Townsend scored a great goal for England, silencing people who had criticized him. The 23-year-old had a difficult season but played well in Italy. England manager Roy Hodgson kept faith in him, and Townsend repaid that trust with a goal that made the score 1-1 against Italy.

Chinese company Dalian Wanda Group has officially bought 20% of the Spanish soccer team Atletico Madrid. The purchase was finalized at a meeting on Tuesday. The team representing Wanda Madrid Investment signed the deal to buy 726,707 shares for €45 million (£32.8m). The deal was first announced in January, but it needed two meetings to be officially completed. Wanda Group chairman Wang Jianlin wants to grow Atletico's brand in Asia. Atletico Madrid manager Diego Simeone speaks to the media.

Antonio Conte returned to Turin for Italy's 1-1 draw against England. He said this brought "very fond memories," even though he received death threats in the days before the friendly.

Conte became Italy's boss in August, replacing Cesare Prandelli after Italy lost its World Cup group-stage last summer. His first seven months in charge have been up and down. Italy needed a late goal from Eder to rescue a 2-2 draw against Bulgaria last Saturday. Conte reportedly received death threats from Juventus fans after Claudio Marchisio suffered a knee injury on the eve of the Euro 2016 qualifier.

Ian Murray thinks that Hibernian can catch Rangers for second place in the Championship. His team, Dumbarton, have played both Rangers and Hibs already this season and will play them again before the season ends. While Rangers are winning at the moment, Murray thinks they might struggle to keep winning. He believes the lead could swing back to Hibs before long.

Liverpool goalkeeper Simon Mignolet returned to England after playing for Belgium in Euro 2016 qualifiers against Cyprus and Israel. Although he was named in Marc Wilmots' match-day squards, he did not play. Chelsea's Thibaut Courtois started instead, keeping Mignolet's cap count at 14. Mignolet shared photos of him posing in an airplane cockpit on Facebook on Wednesday.

A large rural estate is for sale at £6 million. It is near Bridgnorth, Shropshire, and has 200 acres of land. The estate has a Grade II-listed manor house and five cottages. It also has a swimming pool, tennis court, stables, and its own cricket green. The main house, Chyknell Hall, has 11 bedrooms. It was built in 1814 and has only been sold twice before. It is thought that A-list buyers would be attracted to the secluded grounds.

Two college campus police officers in Dallas have been placed on leave after video showed them harassing a group of students and hitting one of them. The incident happened at El Centro College last Wednesday. A student named Charles Adams recorded the video while waiting for a bus outside the campus.

Gary Locke has been made the permanent manager of Kilmarnock. He signed a three-year contract after doing the job temporarily since February. The 39-year-old, who used to work with Allan Johnston, has lost only one game in seven since he took charge. Locke will talk to the media on Friday.

This weekend, one of the biggest games on the German football calendar takes place. Borussia Dortmund and Bayern Munich have won the last five league titles between them, and Bayern are expected to continue their dominance this season.

Usally, these two teams are separated by thirty-one points and nine positions in the league table. However, this gap does not lower the stakes, as the rivalry between these two clubs is always intense.

Jurgen Klop (centre) celebrated with his Borussia Dortmund players after they defeated Hannover.

A 14-year-old girl was left stuck at London Stansted airport after easyJet refused to let her board her flight home to Spain. Deva Joseph was told she could not take her flight because she had two pieces of hand luggage. She offered to pay to have the second bag put in the hold, but was told only credit cards would be accepted, even though she is too young to have one.

Gordon Robson, 26, punched 45-year-old John Potts in the back of the head outside a sports bar. The hit was so hard it made a loud cracking sound, and Mr. Potts fell down and died. Robson, who has a history of violent behavior, was sentenced to three and a half years in prison for the crime that happened in November last year.

Ellen White scored a free kick against her old team, Arsenal. She hit the ball into the corner from the edge of the box. This happened right before halftime. It was a perfect set-piece. For Notts County, it was a great moment.

These are the amazing scenes as high school girls in China are put through their paces with military-style dagger drills. Each of the girls shout the words 'kill, stab, slash and jab' as they perform each of the eight set movements involved in the high-intensity knife-fighting session. According to the People's Daily Online, the girls of the 27th March Huizhou Integrated High School are being trained by former special forces soldier Inspector Tan. The 68 girls involved in the training are all aged between 16 and 18, however in a concession to safety, the knives are not real. School official Huang Anruo said: 'The daggers are fake.'

We spend about a third of our lives sleeping. However, many people do not realize what their mind and body need during these resting hours to feel refreshed every day. According to the Sleep Health Foundation, 30 percent of Australians complain about their lack of sleep daily. Chair Professor David Hillman says these lost hours of sleep must be "paid back" to be functional for the entire week. Studies show that the average adult needs around eight hours of sleep per night, with a recommended range of seven to nine hours.

A video posted on Facebook shows a heated argument between neighbours in a Perth suburb that turned violent. In the clip, an angry woman is heard shouting racist insults over her fence at a group of men who appear to be of African descent. She then goes into her neighbour's front yard with a metal crowbar, shouting at the men and swinging the weapon at them. The men pick up their own weapons and a scuffle breaks out. The woman is heard shouting, "I don't deal with monkeys, go on now you f*****g monkeys."

Everyone is watching Valencia's 19-year-old left back Jose Luis Gaya. Manchester City, Arsenal, and Chelsea want to sign him this summer, but Real Madrid also wants him. Sportsmail's Pete Jenson explains why English clubs are interested. His buy-out clause is £13.5m. Since a similar player, Luke Shaw, cost £27m, it would be silly not to be interested. However, there are also questions about if he is good enough for the Premier League. Jose Luis Gaya played for Valencia during a La Liga match with Sevilla earlier this season.

Police in Oregon are asking the public for help finding a man on a green motorcycle. He saved two teenagers from Edward West, 59, who allegedly threatened them with a gun. The motorcyclist used his helmet to knock the gun out of the man's hands, letting the teens run away.

Tim Sherwood has asked Ron Vlaar to prove himself again now that he is fit and ready to play. Sherwood wants the defender to help Aston Villa avoid relegation. Vlaar was a star player for Holland in last year's World Cup in Brazil, even though he missed a penalty in a shoot-out against Argentina. He is now fit to return for Villa as they play at Old Trafford on Saturday.

Tim Sherwood says he is not worried about a possible takeover of Aston Villa. He plans to build a team for next season if the club stays up in the league. Owner Randy Lerner is in talks to sell the club. But Sherwood is focused on keeping Villa in the league first, before making changes in the summer.

Aston Villa manager Tim Sherwood says he is not worried about a possible takeover. Christian Benteke celebrates scoring against Sunderland last month.

Celtic hoped to keep Jason Denyer on loan from Manchester City next season. However, Manchester City's manager, Manuel Pellegrini, said his young players are not good enough for his first team yet. Because of this, Denyer might have to return to City to fill a gap in their squad. Denyer has done well while playing for Celtic this year on loan from Manchester City.

Southampton manager Ronald Koeman is waiting for a more accurate return date for Fraser Forster before deciding if he needs to sign a new goalkeeper this summer. Forster injured his knee during the 2-0 win over Burnley two weeks ago, and doctors estimate he could be back in four to 12 months. Koeman is hesitant to give a specific timeline but considers Kelvin Davis capable as a backup. However, he may have to strengthen his goalkeeping options if Forster's recovery takes longer.

Rotherham boss Steve Evans was angry on the sidelines after his team were denied a penalty in their narrow Championship defeat at Birmingham. The hosts had led through first-half goals by Robert Tesche and Clayton Donaldson, before Matt Derbyshire pulled one back for fourth-bottom Rotherham. However, Rob Kiernan's clumsy handling of Derbyshire near the hour mark saw the former City forward go down in the box only for referee Dean Whitestone to wave away appeals for a spot-kick, leaving the Millers boss visibly enraged as the home side held out. Robert Tesche of Birmingham City celebrates scoring the opening goal of the game.

The worry about Virgil van Dijk is clear. Holland’s national team has already let in more goals in five Euro 2016 qualifiers than they conceded during the entire qualifying campaign for the last World Cup. And still, Guus Hiddink never calls or writes. The Celtic defender made it into two squads last year. But one step forward is usually followed by two steps back. When the Dutch were drawing 1-1 with Turkey the other night he was sunning himself in the Arabian Gulf and bumping into club-mates instead. Virgil van Dijk has been in fine form for Celtic but wasn't rewarded with a call-up to the Holland national team.

Celtic have complained to the Scottish Football Association (SFA) about ticket prices for their Scottish Cup semi-final against Inverness later this month at Hampden Park.

The SFA has set the prices at £23 for the North and South stands, and £15 for adults and £5 for concessions in the East Stand. The match is scheduled for 12.15pm on Sunday, April 18.

Rangers interim chairman Paul Murray said on Thursday night that previous boardroom leaders were entirely to blame for the club being removed from the stock exchange. The Ibrox team will be forced to leave the Alternative Investment Market (AIM) because they could not find a new nominated advisor to follow the rules. Murray says the new board's future plans are not affected, and promised investments will still happen.

Wayne Rooney and his England teammates were upset by their poor start against Italy on Tuesday night. Nine months after they met at the World Cup, the Three Lions faced the Azzuris again in a friendly match at the Juventus Stadium. Hopes were high after seven straight wins, but Roy Hodgson's men struggled in the first half, falling behind to a Graziano Pelle header. Wayne Rooney gave instructions during the 1-1 draw against Italy on Tuesday night. Rooney said he and the rest of the England players were upset by their first half performance.

Dundee United's two main fan groups are angry about how the club's leaders are doing their job. They are upset that 25 percent of the money made from selling four players—Ryan Gauld, Andrew Robertson, Stuart Armstrong, and Gary Mackay-Steven—went as commission fees to unknown people. The groups also disagree with the chairman's claim about how much money he has put into the club. In response, the board points to the team's good results on the field.

Gary Locke will be announced as Kilmarnock's permanent manager on Friday. He will sign a three-year contract. The 39-year-old former Hearts boss took over the job in February after Allan Johnston left. He has kept the position for eight weeks.

Chinese parents love raising children who are very talented. Some children start school at age 10, and some start dancing at age four. Now, a new basketball star is becoming famous. A video went viral in China showing a small boy with amazing basketball skills. The boy, Mai Zizhuo, is only five years old. He has been playing basketball since he was two and a half years old, according to People's Daily Online. The video shows the boy scoring many baskets and dribbling two balls at the same time.

Bayern Munich will miss David Alaba for the end of the season. The 22-year-old defender got a torn knee ligament while playing for Austria in a 1-1 draw against Bosnia on Tuesday. He is out for about seven weeks. Alaba had a similar injury earlier this season. He said he is disappointed but wants to be back for the season finale.

Hull KR have signed experienced Australian forward Dane Tilse to replace the injured Michael Weyman and Ryan Bailey. The 6ft 7in, 17st-plus Tilse has agreed to a two-and-a-half-year contract and will join the team as soon as paperwork is complete. At 30 years old, Tilse has played 200 games in Australia and will link up with new captain Terry Campese. He is a direct replacement for Weyman, who retired last month due to injury.

Livingston boss Mark Burchill thinks Darren Cole will play in Sunday's final, despite the game happening just one week after his cousin died. Darren's cousin, Shaun Cole, 22, was found dead in a Miami street last weekend. Police believe he was hit by a car. A soldier who served in Afghanistan, Shaun was on holiday in Florida and had been at a music festival before being found injured on a pavement. Mark Burchill is hopeful that Darren will play for Livingston on Sunday.

Alan Smith has denied claims that Liverpool fans attacked the ambulance he was in after he was injured during Manchester United's 1-0 loss to Liverpool nine years ago.

Smith broke his leg and dislocated his ankle while trying to block a free-kick from John Arne Riise in the FA Cup fifth round match at Anfield in February 2006. At the time, reports said Liverpool fans tried to stop Smith's trip to the hospital by throwing bottles, glasses, and stones at the ambulance and rocking the vehicle.

C manager Ronny Deila says Celtic want to sign Hearts captain Danny Wilson this summer. The club is ready to make a £400,000 offer for the defender. Wilson has one year left on his contract with Hearts, but the club does not want to sell him.

Ronny Deila says Celtic will not travel for pre-season games if it risks their Champions League chances. He blames last summer's trip to the US, Austria, and Germany for the 4-1 loss to Legia Warsaw. Celtic makes money from these trips and has visited Australia and Asia recently. Ronny Deila and Nir Bitton left the pitch after the loss. A trip to America this July is not ruled out yet.

Franck Ribery has denied reports that Kevin de Bruyne could replace him or his teammate Arjen Robben at Bayern Munich. De Bruyne, who joined the second-place Bundesliga club from Chelsea two years ago, has had a great season, scoring nine goals and leading the league in assists with 16. However, Ribery says the 23-year-old Belgian player is not the right style of player to come in, because he has different skills than Ribery and the Holland winger.

Following his arrest, Durant, a transfer from a Kansas college and a five-star recruit, was suspended from the football team indefinitely and could be facing expulsion.

Meeting your idol is exciting, but meeting them at Starbucks while wearing a shirt with their name on it, and having your picture posted on their Instagram is even better.

One little boy got to experience this. Justin Verlander, a pitcher for the Detroit Tigers, took a selfie with a little boy who was wearing a dark blue shirt with Verlander's name and number, 35, on the back.

Eden Hazard said that playing too many games for Chelsea and Belgium might have made him too tired to play his best. The 28-year-old has played 48 games this season and missed only five matches for Chelsea. He was an important player as Chelsea chased the Premier League title. But during Belgium's 1-0 win over Israel, manager Marc Wilmots took him off with 28 minutes left. Wilmots said Hazard was struggling against Israel's Orel Dgani.

Police found 20 grams of marijuana hidden inside a leg of lamb in the Northern Territory. The meat was found suspicious by the Northern Substance Abuse Intelligence Desk. Officers x-xaned the lamb and found the drugs. The lamb was sent from Darwin Airport to the Tiwi Islands.

Former Premier League footballer Clarke Carlisle has revealed he has split from his wife of 14 years, Gemma. The couple shared a home in Yorkshire, but Mr. Carlisle has now moved out. This comes as he continues to battle depression following a failed suicide attempt in December. He was arrested on suspicion of drink-driving two days before he tried to kill himself.

Arsenal legend Paul Merson criticized Andros Townsend's England call-up. However, Townsend came off the bench to score an equalizer in Tuesday's 1-1 draw with Italy. This was the perfect riposte to Merson's criticism. Townsend scored England's equaliser in their 1-1 friendly draw with Italy in Turin on Tuesday night. Townsend celebrated his strike with Tottenham Hotspur team-mates Ryan Mason and Kyle Walker.

It seems to be a common trend that Chelsea midfielder Cesc Fabregas struggles in the second half of the season. The Spanish midfielder was one of the worst players in Tuesday's 2-0 defeat against Holland. The 27-year-old said he is happy in west London, but his performance has dropped significantly. Earlier this year, around Christmas, he looked like a sure candidate to break the Barclays Premier League record for assists.

Six people have been arrested in Dover on suspicion of Syria-related terrorism offences. Five men and one woman were detained at around 8:00 this morning in the departure zone of the south coast port. Four of the men are in their 20s and are from Birmingham, West Midlands. A 26-year-old man and a 23-year-old woman with no fixed address were also held. They are currently being questioned at a police station in the West Midlands area.

Arsene Wenger is very respected and clearly very smart. Sometimes, you find yourself nodding along to something he says. It sounds right at first, but closer inspection shows it doesn't have a strong foundation.

Usually, this is about Arsenal's defense. Even after a bad loss, their defensive record is actually very good statistically. But last week, he was talking about quotas. Specifically, FA chairman Greg Dyke's idea to increase the number of homegrown players in a Premier League squad of 25 from eight to 12.

Charlie Austin and Joey Barton are now good friends. When they first met, Barton ignored Austin. However, Austin had a great first season in the league, scoring 15 goals. Because of this, he might get to play for England in the future.

This good dog saved his owner's life. The black dog took a rescue rope to the man at the Clarence J. Brown Dam and Reservoir in Springfield, Ohio, on Saturday afternoon. Firefighters pulled the man to shore after he had spent almost two hours in water that was almost zero degrees Celsius. The man had gotten stuck waist-deep in mud while looking for duck hunting gear. He used his cell phone to call 911. However, first responders could not use a boat because the river was too shallow.

Juventus coach Massimiliano Allegri says he will not be fully accepted by the fans until the team wins the title. He joined Juventus last summer after being sacked by AC Milan. Allegri has done a good job, coaching the team to a strong lead in the race for the Scudetto. Juventus will play Empoli on Saturday looking for three points to stay at the top of the table.

When you are in good shape, it only takes a moment. Nathan Redmond had only been on the field for six minutes when he made the decisive play. Steven Whittaker passed the ball to Redmond on the right side of the field. The ball stayed close to the white line as it moved forward. Redmond ran so fast that he outpaced Joe Bennett. He then crossed the ball high into the net, where Bradley Johnson was waiting at the back post. Bradley Johnson celebrated after scoring the winning goal in the second half at the Amex Stadium.

For six years, residents of Celoron, N.Y., have been upset by a statue of Lucile Ball. In 2009, the town unveiled a statue that looks nothing like the comedian. The face is so unflattering that a Facebook page called 'We Love Lucy! Get Rid of this Statue' has over 600 likes. The statue is based on a famous scene from her show 'I Love Lucy,' where she pitches a health tonic while drunk.

South Sydney hooker Issac Luke is in trouble for a homophobic comment he posted on social media. This happened after Canterbury Bulldogs fans attacked a young Rabbitohs fan at ANZ Stadium in Sydney.

On Saturday, the 27-year-old posted a heartfelt appeal on Instagram to find the fan who was allegedly hurt. Luke had planned to give the fan a jersey for the Easter long weekend to make up for the incident that left the boy in the hospital.

A man in Wangaratta, Australia was shocked when a large spider crawled out of his car door handle. He tried to spray the car with bug spray to make the spider go away. The spider came out and the man told it to get out. The spider ran away scared.

Tottenham manager Mauricio Pochettino says Harry Kane is like Gabriel Batistuta. Kane scored in his first England game, getting close to 30 goals this season. Roy Hodgson is keeping expectations low for Kane, who came back from loans at Leicester and Norwich to make it to the Spurs first-team.

A former footballer who ran a £30 million investment scheme is now living on handouts. Michael McIndoe, who played for Bristol City and Wolverhampton Wanderers, promised footballers a 20 percent return on their money. The scheme collapsed because of debt, and McIndoe was declared bankrupt in October with over £2 million owed. He is known as 'Mr Big' and used to party in Marbella with glamorous women. Now creditors are chasing him through the courts.

Juventus director Pavel Nedved said Barcelona want to sign Paul Pogba. He told a Spanish newspaper that Pogba will not be moving. Nedved was glad Juventus did not play Barcelona in the Champions League.

A 48-year-old man named James Oliver was run over by his girlfriend after she allegedly caught him abusing a 12-year-old girl. Oliver suffered a serious leg injury. Police say the argument happened inside a home in Noblesboro, Maine, after the girlfriend, Linda Currier, 53, caught him trying to sexually assault the young girl. Oliver was found in the driveway on Saturday night.

Liverpool is interested in signing Fiorentina goalkeeper Neto. PSG and Spanish clubs are also interested in him. Brendan Rodgers is having tough competition to get the 25-year-old, whose contract ends in June. Liverpool was linked with a move for Neto earlier in the season when Simon Mignolet was dropped. A January transfer did not happen, but Neto is likely to leave Fiorentina in the summer.

Not everyone should drive a $50,000 car. A YouTube video by Richard Stewart shows a Porsche Cayman speeding from a green light on Prince Edward Island in Canada. The sports car swirled wildly and hit the concrete median. A wheel even came off before the car stopped. Stewart wrote on YouTube, "Just because you have a nice car doesn't make you a good driver. Don't let your son drive your Porsche!"

Here is the information for Sunday's Sunderland versus Newcastle game at the Stadium of Light:

Sunderland's midfielder Lee Cattermole will start in the team. Manager Dick Advocaat said Cattermole is back after he served a two-match ban for getting 10 yellow cards this season.

If Rory McIlroy wins the Masters tournament, he will complete a career grand slam and achieve a lifelong goal as the world's best golfer. Working with his sponsor Bose, McIlroy released a video about his life. The video starts with McIlroy jogging at dawn while the words "Six weeks to Georgia" appear on the screen. It also includes an interview with a young McIlroy before he became a golfing superstar.

Sergio Garcia says he is focused on winning his first PGA Tour title since 2012 at this week's Shell Houston Open. This is happening even though the Masters tournament is coming up soon. For the last few weeks, people have been talking about Rory McIlroy trying to win a third major in a row to complete the career grand slm. They have also been wondering if Tiger Woods will end his self-imposed break from playing. But, even though the Golf Club of Houston is set up to try to copy the conditions players will face at Augusta, Garcia is just concentrating on ending his victory drought. Sergio Garcia lines up a putt during the Cadillac Championship in Doral, Florida last month.

Riki Hughes, a veteran of the Iraq war, went to jail for 16 months. He stole £17,000 from Tidworth Town Football Club, where he volunteered as secretary. Hughes claimed he was paying the club's landlord rent, but the team actually got the property for free. He used the stolen money for his own expenses, including camping equipment and a stag night do in Las Vegas.
Johnny Sexton is very successful. He has won trophies every year since he started playing at a high level, except for 2010. He is getting ready for a big game in Paris against Saracens.

Mustafa Kamal stepped down as ICC president on Wednesday. He accused India of changing the result of the Cricket World Cup quarter-final match between Bangladesh and India. He said everyone saw what happened during that game and that India used its position to influence the outcome. Kamal, who is from Bangladesh, said that if this happened to any other country, he would have reacted the same way. He is now a former ICC president.

West Ham manager Sam Allardyce supports Nigel Pearson. He says he admires the Leicester City boss for being "his own man." Allardyce hired Pearson as a coach at Newcastle United in 2007. The two will meet again on Saturday when West Ham plays Leicester.

Pearson has had some controversial moments this season. He grabbed Crystal Palace player James McArthur by the throat. He also lost his cool with a reporter during a press conference.

Skipper John O'Shea has asked Sunderland to win their next game to keep control of their own survival. Sunderland and Newcastle meet at the Stadium of Light on Sunday. Sunderland has won the last four games in a row of derbies, but they need three points to move away from the bottom of the table. If Burnley beat Tottenham before the game, Sunderland could find themselves in the relegation zone. O'Shea and his team-mates know that three points are a necessity.

Stoke boss Mark Hughes wants to end the team's bad record at Chelsea. Since getting promoted to the Premier League in 2008, Stoke has played Chelsea away eight times and lost every game. Their last win at Chelsea was a League Cup win in 1995. The last time Stoke got a point at Chelsea was a 1-1 draw in 1984. Stoke manager Mark Hughes says his team must end this bad run. Frank Lampard celebrated as Chelsea beat Stoke 3-0 on their most recent visit.

Newcastle will play Sunderland in a big derby game on Sunday. The team is trying to avoid losing three games in a row. They are missing their banned striker, Papiss Cisse. Sunderland are doing poorly at the bottom of the league, sitting just above the drop zone. However, without Cisse’s goals, Newcastle would be two points lower than Sunderland in the relegation zone. Cisse is Newcastle’s top scorer this season with 11 goals. Ten of those goals have helped the team win games.

Dick Advocaat is bringing back Lee Cattermole to the main part of his Sunderland team. Cattermole, 27, has been out of the last two games because he got too many yellow cards. However, he is fit to play against Newcastle on Sunday. Advocaat wants Cattermole to do well, as the player has missed a lot of the season because of injuries.

For Ronny Deila, playing in the Champions League is not just about the money. However, there are now 16 million reasons for the Norwegian manager to guide Celtic to a fourth straight title.

Last year, when Celtic played in the Champions League group stage, they won one match and earned 12.6 million pounds. If they perform that well again, that sum could rise by 4 million. If they reach the last 16, the money would pass 20 million. This is all before they even count ticket sales.

Tottenham defender Ben Davies will play against his teammate Sam Vokes at Burnley on Sunday. Spurs are going to Turf Moor after winning one game out of four, since their loss to Manchester United. They want to keep their hopes of European qualification alive. Burnley are currently 18th in the league, just one point from safety, and they are fighting to stay in the league.

Neil Redfearn is thinking about his job as manager of Leeds United after the club suspended his assistant, Steve Thompson. Leeds United hired Thompson only two months ago, but they told him in a letter from director of football Nicola Salerno that he is suspended until the end of the season. This effectively ends his time at the club after 105 days. Thompson has been told his suspension will last until his contract expires. He has also been told the club will not renew his contract.

John Carver says he will use a whip if he has to in a bid to motivate his Newcastle players ahead of Sunday’s Tyne-Wear derby at the Stadium of Light. The Magpies have lost the last four matches against their North-East rivals and head coach Carver – who was assistant to Alan Pardew during that wretched run – admits that Sunderland wanted victory more than United on those occasions. ‘In the last four games Sunderland have out-worked us - and that's not a good stat to have,’ he said. John Carver says he will 'whip' his players to make sure they're motivated to beat Sunderland on Sunday .

David Templeton has strongly criticized the training methods used at Rangers under Ally McCoist and Kenny McDowall. He believes Stuart McCall's approach is better. Templeton praised McCall for the positive impact he has had since joining the team last month, noting that two recent wins have boosted confidence before the match against Hearts.

Nolito, a forward for Celta Vigo, says Lionel Messi should go to the beach instead of playing in their La Liga match on Sunday. Messi has a minor foot injury, but he is expected to recover in time for the game. Nolito, 28, told a newspaper, "I guess he'll come, but he can spend the day at the beach as far as I'm concerned. I'll give his dad a ring in a minute."

Robbie Neilson says that captain Danny Wilson will only leave Hearts if he thinks it is the right move for the club. Earlier this week, reports showed that Celtic have been watching Wilson, who used to play for Rangers. Neilson says that other teams wanting his players is normal, but he will not sell anyone unless the price is right.

Sam Allardyce has warned Brendan Rodgers that giving Raheem Sterling a big new contract could cause a problem for the rest of the Liverpool team. The West Ham manager feels that paying Sterling more than the £100,000-per-week deal he was already offered would lead to the 20-year-old's team-mates demanding more. Yet Allardyce does not blame Sterling, currently on £35,000 a week at Liverpool, for trying to get as much as possible. Big Sam feels there are so few talented youngsters emerging that clubs are willing to pay extraordinary wages to sign any available. Liverpool and England star Raheem Sterling has stalled over signing a new contract at the Anfield club.

Blackpool is trying to sign 25-year-old defender Thomas Piermayr. The player, who is from Austria, is currently a free agent. He used to play for Colorado Rapids and had a spell with Inverness Caledonian Thistle in 2011. Blackpool wants to sign him for what is expected to be a season in League One next year. This would be the defender's first chance to play in England.

Tony Pulis wants to talk to West Bromwich Albion's chairman, Jeremy Peace, after the team stays safe from relegation to make the club a top-ten team again. Pulis says the team has "g gone off the rails" recently and needs big changes to get back on track. West Brom finished 10th and 8th under previous managers Roy Hodgson and Steve Clarke, but struggled to stay safe last season and finished 17th.

Arsenal legend Ian Wright is sad to see Theo Walcott leave the club. He thinks Walcott's problems are because manager Arsene Wenger wouldn't play him as a striker. Walcott has only started five games this season after coming back from a knee injury. With Arsenal looking for new players like Raheem Sterling and Walcott's contract ending next summer, Wright worries the team might lose a good player.

Roberto Martinez is confident that Ross Barkley will become a better player for Everton and England. Barkley had a mixed season because he was part of England's World Cup squad last summer and had knee surgery. However, England manager Roy Hodgson still believes in him. Martinez thinks Barkley is ready to play well again after he came off the bench for England in the last two games.

England will not play in the Under 19 European Championships this summer. The Young Lions lost 2-1 to France in their final qualifier. They had beaten Denmark and Azerbaijan in earlier rounds, but needed to beat France to advance. Goals from Sehrou Guirassy and Gnaly Cornet put France in command. A late goal from Patrick Roberts was not enough to qualify the team.

Newcastle midfielder Jonas Gutierrez is hoping to celebrate his return to the team with a win over struggling Sunderland. The 31-year-old Argentinian has come on as a substitute in the last three games since returning from cancer. He has been welcomed back warmfully. However, he has lost each of those games. He is desperate to end that run as Newcastle tries to bounce back from four successive defeats by their rivals on Sunday.

NRL referees and officials were hit by plastic water bottles and abuse from angry fans after South Sydney beat Canterbury 18-17 in a close match. The Rabbitohs won when the Bulldogs' captain was penalized in the final minute. As the game ended, fans threw bottles and shouted at the referees and players as they left the field.

Former England captain Kevin Sinfield has been warned he will be a 'target' when he switches to rugby union at the end of the season. Sinfield, 34, the greatest captain in Leeds' history, stunned the world of rugby league on Tuesday with his sudden announcement that he will quit the sport at the end of the season and join the Rhinos' sister club Yorkshire Carnegie on an 18-month contract. Leeds Rhinos captain Kevin Sinfield is to switch codes and join Yorkshire Carnegie at the end of the season.

Raheem Sterling, a 20-year-old player for Liverpool, has said he is not ready to sign a new contract. The club offered him £100,000-a-week to stay, but he says he would have signed for less money a year ago.

Although he is a important player for Liverpool, his form has been poor this season. He has scored only six goals, which is one less than Jon Walters of Stoke. His scoring rate has also gotten worse.

Brighton and Hove Albion are the first club to give young players training on the law and ethics of sexual consent. The program, called Protect, Inform and Prevent (PIP), explains when consent can be given legally. The training includes confidential question and answer sessions led by a former police detective and a psychotherapist.

A new video shows homeless people reading out cruel tweets written about them. The clip was made by the creative agency Leo Burnett Toronto for the homeless charity Humans For Humans. It is designed to make people think about how they treat people who sleep rough. Many of the people break down in tears as they read comments like, 'I hate the homeless, I don’t feel sorry for you,' and 'I saw a homeless girl across the street. I almost vomited.'

George Boyd is the Barclays Premier League's hardest working player. He has run a total of 210.5 miles on the pitch this season. This distance is the equivalent of running from Burnley's Turf Moor ground to Crystal Palace's Selhurst Park in south London. The Burnley winger has run slightly further than Tottenham Hotspur midfielder Christian Eriksen. Walking the journey from Turf Moor to Selhurst would usually take 69 hours, according to Google Maps' estimations, but Boyd has managed it in less than 40 hours of playing time.

Police are investigating the death of a five-month-old baby. The child's parents, a 25-year-old father and a 25-year-old mother from Perry Barr, Birmingham, have been arrested.

Emergency services were called to their home just before 1:00 AM yesterday because the baby was having breathing difficulties. The baby was taken to Birmingham Children's Hospital, but doctors could not save her, and she was pronounced dead this afternoon.

A police spokesman said the death is being treated as suspicious. A post-mortem examination is scheduled to take place today to determine the exact cause of death.

Gordon Taylor, the head of the players' union, says Raheem Sterling is not being greedy by waiting to talk about a new contract. The 20-year-old England player has been given a huge new offer, believed to be 100,000 pounds a week, but talks have stopped. Sterling has said he is not just after money, and Taylor believes it is smart to wait until the season ends before talking again. Sterling also told TV that he is not ready to sign a new deal with Liverpool yet.

Things have been bad for Manchester United flop Anderson since he went back to Brazil. On Wednesday, his own mistakes were outshown by a teammate's mistake. The Brazilian midfielder was sent off after shoving an opponent. His opponent was also sent off for hitting back with an elbow. But Anderson was lucky because his colleague Fabricio stole the spotlight by swearing at his own fans. He became the third player sent off, reducing Internacional to nine men in the 1-1 draw in Porto Alegre.

A seven-year-old boy was raped and set on fire by two youths when he went to buy food. The youths took the boy to an isolated place and raped him. When he resisted, they set him on fire. The boy suffered 30 per cent burns to his body, but somehow managed to escape. The shocking incident occurred in Pagma Nagar, in Bhiwandi City, a suburb of Mumbai. Police are investigating the incident.

A pug named Dug had a lucky recovery after a rattlesnake bit him in the face. Dug and his owner, Lindsay Castro, were hiking on the Jurupa Hills trail in Fontana, California, on Thursday. They heard a rattling sound. Lindsay moved back, but Dug ran up to the snake instead. The snake bit Dug in the face, and his face instantly swelled up to twice its size.

Dug is a curious pup who got bitten while investigating a sound while hiking. His face got very big, but he is okay now.

Jose Mourinho could one day return to manage Real Madrid, even though he left the club in 2013. Real defender Alvaro Arbeloa says the door is open for the Chelsea manager to come back.

Mourinho spent three years at Real Madrid before he left to rejoin Chelsea. He left amid rumors of arguments with star players like Iker Casillas, Sergio Ramos, and Pepe. But Arbeloa, who has played 25 games this season, says Real Madrid would welcome Mourinho back as manager.

Liverpool and their manager Brendan Rodgers had a tough day at the Emirates on Saturday. Their hopes of playing in the Champions League next year are over. The manager’s 15-minute press conference felt like a sad goodbye, as he admitted his team had missed out of the title race. Rodgers tried to stay positive, but he was honest that this season has been hard. Last year, Liverpool fought hard for the championship, but this year they have fallen back. It is hard for fans to accept, especially after they hoped for a return to winning ways. Even though they lost, it still feels like Liverpool are moving forward under Rodgers.

Angry Inter Milan coach Roberto Mancini cancelled his players' day off and ordered them to train early Sunday morning after they tied 1-1 at home with bottom-of-the-table Parma. Inter's website says the team trained at 8:30 a.m. local time, watched by vice-president Javier Zanetti and sporting director Piero Ausilio. Mancini was furious at his players' attitude after the Saturday's draw left them joint ninth alongside Genoa and 10 points adrift of the European places. Roberto Mancini has cancelled his Inter Milan players' day off on Easter and ordered them into training.

F fans want to own a piece of sports history, and small items connected to famous players or teams can sell for thousands of dollars. But you might be surprised to learn that an expired passport belonging to Paul Parker, a famous right-back for Manchester United and England in the 90s, was listed on eBay for 5,000 pounds. The item was listed in March, and the bidding ended on Tuesday, but it is unclear if anyone actually paid that price. Paul Parker's old passport was listed on eBay.

A builder named Paddy Morrall found a piece of wood that looked like Jesus Christ. He saw the image in a loft of toast, pancakes, and ice cream, but was especially surprised to see it on a wooden board in Scotland just before Easter.

The wood was left out in the rain, and the image of Jesus appeared. Mr. Morrall, a 31-year-old man from Keighley, has kept the piece of wood.

Ondrej Duda scored one goal in the second half to give Slovakia a 1-0 win over the Czech Republic on Tuesday. The 20-year-old midfielder scored with a low shot from outside the penalty area in the 49th minute. It was Slovakia's third win in ten games since the countries split in 1993. Martin Skrtel hit Daniel Kolar in the face with a high boot during the match.

Real Madrid star Karim Benzema showed off his rapping skills while driving his Bugatti Veyron. As Madrid prepare to play Granada on Sunday, he shared a video singing along to Tupac's song 'Check Out Time'. Even though Tupac's song 'All Eyez on Me' might have been a better choice, Benzema is focused on adding to his 20 goals this season.

A businessman who helped force Liam Fox to resign is spending money to defeat two Conservative politicians.

Harvey Boulter has given £30,000 to a Ukip candidate fighting against Liam Fox in Somerset. He is also spending another £30,000 to try to defeat Tom Tugendhat, a Conservative candidate in Kent.

In the last four minutes of the game, two goals were scored, making the match between Sheffield Wednesday and Huddersfield end in a 1-1 draw. Sheffield Wednesday's substitute Sergiu Bus scored first in the 86th minute. Huddersfield's substitute Ishmael Miller scored just before the game ended to tie the score. This result means Huddersfield has not won in their last seven games, and they are in 18th position, nine and six points behind Wednesday. Sergiu Bus celebrating his goal against Huddersfield.

Stuart Dallas has come a long way since Mark Warburton found him playing part-time for Crusaders back home for only £70-a-week. The 23-year-old, who impressed for Northern Ireland, scored two excellent goals as Brentford demolished Fulham 4-1 on Good Friday. They go into Monday's game against Nottingham Forest eyeing more than just a play-off spot. It was three years ago when Dallas was spotted by Warburton playing part-time on a mud bath for Crusaders back home. Stuart Dallas celebrates the second of his two excellent goals against Fulham on good Friday. Dallas has been a revelation this season as he helps Brentford push towards the Premier League.

Baseball is very popular in America. Because of this, people have very strong feelings about their favorite professional teams. The New York Yankees and Boston Red Sox are the most popular teams, coming in first and second place. Other teams with many fans include the Texas Rangers and the Atlanta Braves. Some teams, like the New York Mets, are less popular.

Trey Moses, a senior at Eastern High School in Louisville, Kentucky, asked Ellie Meredith to be his date to the upcoming prom. Moses, who volunteers with teenagers with learning disabilities, surprised her during her P.E. class with a bunch of flowers and a sign reading: 'Let's Party Like it's 1989' - a reference to an album by Taylor Swift, Ellie's favorite singer. Ellie accepted the promposal and said she can't wait to go dress shopping 'because I've only told about a million people!' she told CNN.

On April Fools' Day, President Barack Obama pretended to be Frank Underwood, the main character from the TV show House of Cards.

He said, "Hello everybody. This is not Frank Underwood. This is Barack Obama. Happy April Fools' Day. Frank learned it from me."

President Obama used a southern accent to impersonate the character, who is usually played by actor Kevin Spacey and is known for giving long speeches to the TV audience.

Caykur Rizespor midfielder Ludovic Obraniak went to the hospital on Saturday after being taken off during the match against Fenerbahce. The Poland international was substituted after 30 minutes for tests. The club posted on social media that Obraniak was not in immediate danger after the preliminary tests. He is currently on loan at Caykur Rizespor from German side Werder Bremen. Fenerbahce player Moussa Sow scored during their 5-1 win on Saturday.

Three people went to the hospital after a crash between a classic 1973 Jaguar and a Toyota Kluger on Easter Sunday night in Frenchs Forest. The vintage car was badly damaged. Police are still investigating the accident.

Villagers in Shandong Province, China, have started carrying natural gas in large plastic bags. Photos from Lijin village show people transporting the gas on rickshaws. Because the gas is very fl dangerous, onlookers compare this to carrying a bomb. Local media reports that people do this to save money on gas costs.

Tiger Woods has been seen practicing at Augusta National, which increases the chances he will play in this year's first Major tournament. Woods has not played on the PGA Tour since he withdrew from the Farmers Insurance Open on February 5 due to back problems. He has since taken a leave of absence to try to get back into shape, but there is speculation he will return for the Masters, a tournament he has won four times. Tiger Woods was spotted practicing at Augusta on Tuesday, and he is said to have returned to the course. Woods has dropped out of the top 100 for the first time in almost 19 years.

The BBC has faced criticism for using licence fee payers' money to pay for a guide teaching staff how to use emojis. The corporation spent thousands of pounds on a 44-page document. An agency was hired to research how to use smiley faces in news stories and on social media. The guide also included instructions on how to draw emoji faces for popular stars like Gary Lineker and Graham Norton. The BBC was later seen using a 'sad face' emoticon to describe the death of the world's oldest woman.

One of the world's top distance runners says he is living in fear after telling police in Uganda that a coach sexually abused young female runners, some as young as 15.

Moses Kipsiro, a training partner of Mo Farah's and a Commonwealth Games champion, says five runners came to him for help. He reported the allegations to his national federation and police, and now claims he has received death threats.

Patrick Kluivert, a former Dutch player and assistant coach, has started his job as Curacao's coach with two wins. Curacao won 2-1 on Saturday and drew 2-2 on Tuesday to advance to the second round of World Cup qualifying by beating Montserrat 4-3 on total points. Kluivert, who worked with coach Louis van Gaal at the 2014 World Cup, has helped Curacao progress to the next stage of qualifying for the 2018 tournament.

An 18-year-old student has been kicked out of his fraternity, left college, and been sent for a mental health check-up after video showed him bite a live hamster's head off.

DailyMail.com found Brady Eaves, the stepson of a former Mississippi governor candidate, in a video from a drunken Spring Break party. The footage, allegedly filmed in Florida, shows the teenager laughing as he kills the small animal. He could face felony animal cruelty charges, which carry a maximum jail term of five years and $5,000 in fines.

Sri Lanka's sports minister asked Kumar Sangakkara to play one more year of limited overs cricket. Sangakkara had just retired after a quarter-final loss in the World Cup, saying he was happy with how the team had improved since 2000. The minister made this request while introducing a new group to run the sport.

Edinburgh have recalled three Scottish international players for their European Challenge Cup quarter-final against London Irish on Sunday.

Dougie Fife, Alasdair Dickinson, and Ross Ford were all rested during Scotland's win over Scarlets last week, after they played in the RBS Six Nations. They are back in the squad as head coach Alan Solomons looks to pick his strongest starting team.

Dougie Fife is one of three Scottish players returning to Edinburgh after playing in the Six Nations.

Chris Ramsey says Tony Pulis is one of the best British coaches. He says he doesn't need to take any tactical tips from Pulis. Ramsey's QPR are 19th in the league, four points away from 17th place Sunderland. The R’s have only taken four points since the turn of the year. They could do with a season climax reminiscent of Pulis’s 2013-14 campaign with Crystal Palace, in which they took 17 points from their final eight games to avoid the drop.

An 18-year-old student named Silhan Ozcelik appeared in court. She is accused of planning to travel abroad to join Kurdish rebels fighting the Islamic State. Ozcelik, who is a sixth-form student, disappeared from her family's home in north London last October while she was still 17. Prosecutors say she traveled to Stuttgart, Germany, on the Eurostar with another man. They allege she went there to join the PKK youth movement.
